newsitem.title: USA: Delta sees Q2 unit costs lower than Q1.
newsitem.headline: Delta sees Q2 unit costs lower than Q1.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc said as a result of continued efforts to keep costs under control, unit costs for its second quarter, which ended December 31, will be slightly lower than those of the previous quarter and below earlier expectations.
The company also said that it saw particularly strong growth in "other" revenues, including sales of frequent flier miles and targeted marketing programs, in the December quarter.
It said non-passenger revenues for the December 1996 quarter grew at a year-over-year rate similar to the September 1996 quarter, exceeding earlier expectations.

"We are very pleased that despite exceptional traffic growth and higher fuel prices in the quarter, our operating cost per available seat mile will be down slightly from the September 1996 quarter," said Thomas Roeck, Delta's chief financial officer.
"These results reflect our intention to maintain our standing as the lowest cost U.S. hub and spoke carrier."
Delta said it will release earnings for the December quarter on January 23.
